title: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Heritage Listing for the Bight) Bill 2018
short_title: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Heritage Listing for the Bight) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require a defined Commonwealth area of the Great Australian Bight to be placed permanently on Australia’s National Heritage List under federal environmental legislation.
The minister would list the area and its actual or possible heritage values, after consulting affected communities in South Australia and Western Australia about those values.
The amendments would begin on Royal Assent and cover the specified Southern Ocean area within Australia’s continental shelf, excluding areas associated with external territories.
changes: A dedicated statutory process would require the minister to add the Bight heritage area to the list.
The minister would have to consult affected communities before recording heritage values.
The listed area could not later be removed from the National Heritage List.
summary.affected: The environment minister and communities in South Australia and Western Australia likely to be affected by listing are affected.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Heritage Listing for the Bight) Bill 2018 to grant National Heritage status to the Great Australian Bight, citing 74% community support and arguing that oil drilling poses catastrophic risks, with Equinor's worst-case discharge estimates of up to 7.9 million barrels.
